title: Uncovering the structure of self-regulation through data-driven ontology discovery
authors: Ian W. Eisenberg, Patrick G. Bissett, A. Zeynep Enkavi, Jamie Li, David P. MacKinnon, Lisa A. Marsch, Russell A. Poldrack
caption_short: Schematic of a directed-forgetting trial: fixation, six letters in two rows (2.5 s), a TOP / BOT cue to forget one row (1 s), a 3 s delay, then a probe letter to judge as in or not in the remaining memory set.
notes: Drawn by us: none of the papers describing this dataset has a figure of this task. Eisenberg et al. 2019 (Nat Commun, CC BY 4.0) has only analysis figures (Fig. 1a lists 'Directed forgetting' among task names); Enkavi et al. 2019 (PNAS) shows reliability results only; the Experiment Factory paper (Sochat et al. 2016, Front Psychol 7:610) shows software diagrams only. Task details are taken from the task code that ran the study (github.com/expfactory/expfactory-experiments, MIT licence, directed_forgetting/experiment.js): 1 s red fixation, six letters in a 2 x 3 layout for 2.5 s, cue image TOP or BOT for 1 s ('forget the top / bottom letters'), 3 s red fixation, probe letter for 2 s (left arrow = in the memory set, right arrow = not), 4 s inter-trial fixation; probe types pos / pos / neg / con repeated, i.e. half memory-set letters, a quarter from the row to forget, a quarter new letters; 8 practice trials with feedback, 3 runs of 24 test trials. The letters drawn are an example, not from a real trial; in the real task the letters are images of capital letters. Rendered with Pillow (DejaVu Sans).
